detail:
NIDDK describes type 2 diabetes as the most common type of diabetes, a disease that occurs when blood glucose, also called blood sugar, is too high. In type 2 diabetes, the cells in the body do not use insulin properly, a pattern called insulin resistance, and the pancreas may not make enough insulin to keep glucose in the usual range. NIDDK lists risk factors that can include overweight or obesity, family history, age, and lack of physical activity.

Symptoms can include increased thirst and urination, fatigue, blurred vision, and slow-healing sores, and NIDDK notes they often develop slowly over years and may be mild enough to go unnoticed. Clinicians usually diagnose type 2 diabetes with blood tests such as the A1C test, fasting plasma glucose, or an oral glucose tolerance test, often confirming a result with repeat testing unless symptoms are clear. Evaluation also commonly includes blood pressure, cholesterol, and screening for eye, kidney, and nerve complications.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about type 2 diabetes symptoms and diagnosis.

title: Type 2 diabetes: when cells stop responding well to insulin
